title: Thailand Clothes to Wear: Temple-Ready, Market-Ready Outfits for Women
seo_title: Thailand Clothes to Wear: Temples, Markets and Heat
meta_description: Thailand clothes to wear for heat, temples, markets and Bangkok nights: what to pack, how to cover up with respect, and how Thai pieces travel home.
excerpt: Temple rules, market days, cold malls and island evenings: a packing list for Thailand, plus what modern and traditional Thai clothes look like.

hero.intro: Thailand clothes to wear come down to two things: heat and respect. You want fabric that breathes, and enough cover to walk into a temple without a second thought. This guide takes you through temples, markets, malls, islands and Bangkok nights, then shows what women in Thailand actually wear.

sections.heading: Thailand clothes to wear start with the heat
paragraphs: Plan for warm and sticky. Most of the country runs hot and humid for much of the year. The rainy months bring short, heavy downpours, often in the afternoon. The north can turn cool at night in the cooler months, so pack one warm layer if you are heading up there. Everywhere else, the real question is how fast your clothes dry.

So pick the fabric before the outfit. Linen, cotton and viscose let air through and dry quickly. Thick denim and heavy polyester hold heat and stay damp for hours. Loose cuts beat tight ones, because cloth that skims the body moves air instead of trapping it. Pale colors stay cooler in the sun, but thin white cotton can turn see-through in the rain. Most thailand clothes for women on a smart packing list are light, loose and easy to rinse in a sink.

sections.heading: Temples: cover shoulders and knees
paragraphs: Temples are the part with real rules. Cover your shoulders and your knees, and skip anything sheer or very tight. Those two lines shape most thailand clothes to wear on a sightseeing day. The big royal sites in Bangkok check clothes at the gate, so that is the one place not to improvise. Smaller temples may say nothing, but the rule still stands, and following it is simple courtesy.

Plan for bare feet, too. You take your shoes off before you step into a temple building, so slip-on sandals save time all day. Inside, sit with your feet tucked to one side and never point them at a Buddha image. Women should not touch a monk or hand him something directly. Leave clothes with Buddha images printed on them at home.
bullets: A midi or maxi skirt, or wide trousers past the knee.
A top with sleeves, or a light shirt worn open over a tank.
A large scarf in your bag as a back-up shoulder cover.
Sandals you can slip off and on in seconds.

sections.heading: Markets: dress for a long walk
paragraphs: Markets mean hours on your feet. Wear flat shoes you have already broken in, and carry a small bag across your body so both hands stay free. Night markets stay warm after dark, so cotton and linen still win. A skirt with pockets or a light pair of trousers keeps cash and a phone close.

Expect few fitting rooms. Many stalls sell clothes as "free size", one size meant to fit most, and the cut often runs small. Wear a slim tank or a fitted tee you can try things over. Then hold a piece up against a top you know fits. Our guide to bangkok clothes shopping covers how markets and malls work, from bargaining to sizes.

sections.heading: Malls and nights out in Bangkok
paragraphs: Bring a layer into the city. Malls, trains and cinemas run the air conditioning hard, and the jump from hot street to cold hall is real. A light cardigan or a long shirt in your bag solves it. That tip holds whether you head to Bangkok Fashion Island or any of the city's other big malls.

Bangkok clothes also run neater than beach clothes. People in the city tend to dress tidy, even in the heat. Some rooftop bars and smarter restaurants ask for smart casual, which usually means no flip-flops and no beachwear. A linen dress with flat sandals, or wide trousers with a silky top, works almost anywhere after dark. If you searched "bangkok thailand clothes" for a night out, that is the formula.

sections.heading: Islands and beaches: swimwear stays on the sand
paragraphs: The islands feel relaxed, but the same courtesy travels with you. Keep swimwear for the beach and the pool. Pull on a dress, a shirt or a sarong before you walk into town, a shop or a cafe. Topless sunbathing is not part of local beach life, so leave it out.

Sun is the bigger issue here. A wide hat, a light long-sleeved shirt and a loose cover-up do more than sunscreen alone. Pack one dress that goes from beach to dinner, in a fabric that shrugs off sand and salt. For more holiday outfits, our vacation outfit ideas work just as well on a Thai island.

sections.heading: Chic travel clothes for women: one small bag
paragraphs: Pack less and wear it more. The best chic travel clothes for women mix and match, so every top works with every bottom. Stick to two or three colors that get along. Then one bag covers temple mornings, market afternoons and dinner. The list below holds all the thailand clothes to wear for a week or two. If you are petite, a search for "petite dresses linen" is a good start, because a hem that lands below your knee does the temple job too. See our petite dresses for cuts and lengths.
bullets: Two midi skirts, one plain and one printed, from our skirts.
One pair of wide linen or cotton trousers.
Three tops: a sleeved blouse, a fitted tee, a silky shell.
One long shirt to wear open as a light layer.
One linen or cotton dress for day and night.
Flat sandals, walking shoes and a large scarf.

sections.heading: Modern thai clothes and the Bangkok scene
paragraphs: Bangkok dresses well. Modern thai clothes lean toward clean cuts, soft colors, playful prints and a lot of linen. Many university students still wear a uniform, a white blouse with a dark skirt, so you see neat, simple shapes everywhere. The word for fashion in Thai comes from English and sounds much the same, which tells you how freely the city mixes ideas.

We won't name a thai fashion brand here. The scene moves fast, and a small thai clothes brand may sell from a market stall, a mall pop-up or its own online shop. Read the label the same way anywhere: fabric, flat measurements and whether "free size" means your size. Our thai fashion page shows the pieces we bring back from Thailand.

sections.heading: Traditional Thai dress, worn with respect
paragraphs: Traditional dress comes out for weddings, festivals, temple days and photos at old cities. Traditional thai clothes for women center on a tube skirt or a wrapped skirt, a fitted blouse and a shoulder cloth draped on the diagonal. Traditional thai clothes men wear include a wrapped lower cloth tucked through the legs, and a shirt with a short standing collar. Renting a set for photos at a historic temple is common, and people welcome it.

Hmong thai clothes are a different thing. The Hmong are an ethnic group with villages in the hills of northern Thailand, and in Laos, Vietnam and southern China too. Their pleated skirts, indigo batik and fine stitching belong to them, so buy from Hmong makers where you can. If you searched thailand clothes traditional, our guide to traditional thai clothes names every piece and covers traditional thai fashion you can wear on a normal day.

faqs.q: What are the best thailand clothes to wear in the rainy season?
faqs.a: Quick-drying linen, cotton and viscose, in loose cuts. Pick sandals that can get wet and dry fast, and skip thick denim, which stays damp for hours. Thin white cotton can turn see-through in a downpour, so a print or a mid tone is safer. A light rain jacket or a compact umbrella in your bag covers the short, heavy showers.

faqs.q: Can I wear leggings or shorts to a temple?
faqs.a: Shorts that stop above the knee are out at most temples. Leggings on their own can count as too tight, and the big royal sites turn away sheer clothing too. The safe choice is a loose midi or maxi skirt, or wide trousers, with a top that covers your shoulders. Carry a large scarf as a back-up, since a few smaller temples have nothing to lend.

faqs.q: What about thailand clothes for men?
faqs.a: The same rules apply. For temples he needs trousers or long shorts that cover the knee, and a shirt with sleeves, not a tank top. Linen and cotton beat heavy fabric, and slip-on shoes help. We sell womenswear only, so on thai clothes for men we can offer advice, not stock.

faqs.q: How do I pack Thai pieces to travel home?
faqs.a: Roll linen and cotton rather than folding them, and expect a few creases. A short steam in a hot shower fixes most of them. Wrap silk in a soft cloth and hand-wash it cool once you are home. Leave a little room in your bag on the way out, because most people come back with more than they took.
